rationale: JLS 4.4 — a DECLARED type variable is a declaration, so it must be a symbol. Before this fixture the analyzer read every one of them (genericParameters: ["K","V"] on the class symbol) and emitted `references` edges TO those strings, while publishing ZERO symbols of kind `type` — so every `references -> K` named a declaration that existed nowhere in the index. Measured on the whole corpus (3,275 .java files, all parsed): 9,780 type_parameter nodes over 1,543 files; on a 250-file store slice, references->V 815 and references->K 773 rows with target_symbol_id NULL, 59.5% of all unresolved references targets. Pins: (a) one SymbolKind.Type symbol per declared variable, at every position that can declare one — class, method, nested class, interface; (b) the `contains` edge that says which declaration owns it, at confidence 1.0, on the VARIABLE's own line; (c) the existing `references` edges still fire and still name the variable. The kind is `type` because src/ast/types.ts:18 declares SymbolKind.Type, parallel-indexer's CONTAINER_TYPES_LOOKUP already treats `type` as a container, and this analyzer's own resolveEnclosingTypeScope already tests for it. The name stays BARE (`K`, not `Cache.K`) on purpose: a `references -> K` edge names `K`, so publishing the symbol qualified would leave every one of those edges unresolved again, which is the defect being fixed.
